page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / A room with a view
title: A room with a view
description:
The team at Tip Top Trading has lots to do, but now Anna has discovered she has to organise a launch party for the new plastic aubergine. It's taking place at the end of the week and nobody has organised a venue yet! Anna is going to need some help.
This episode focuses on the language that you might when trying to book a venue for a business meeting or a product launch.
phrases: Could I check availability for your venue please?
What business facilities do you have?
How many people can the room or venue hold?

listening_challenge.question: What does the room that Marge offers Anna have a view of?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again and welcome to English at Work. The team at Tip Top Trading has lots to do, but now Anna has discovered she has to organise a launch party for the new plastic aubergine. It’s taking place at the end of the week and nobody has organised a venue yet! I think Anna is going to need some help.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So Anna, I’m sorry Tom didn't tell you but do you think you can turn something round by Friday?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'll try, but what do I need to do?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh not much, book a room somewhere, send out some invites… arrange some food… and drink… that sort of thing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's all?!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You can do it - you're great at this kind of thing. And get the team to help.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I'll give it a go. See you later.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thanks Anna. And don't forget to order some of those posh Belgian chocolate biscuits, they always go down well with the clients.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear Anna. It looks like you have your work cut out.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Cut out?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I mean, you have a difficult job to do - but as Paul says, you can do it.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Are you OK Anna? You look a bit worried.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I am. You forgot to tell me about the product launch on Friday and now Paul wants me to organise it.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Did I? Oh sorry. Look, if I can help in any way, just let me know.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, you could book a venue for the launch.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Ahh yeah… just remembered, I've got some Imperial Lemons I need to send out. Maybe later, yeah?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: How am I going to find a venue for the launch at such short notice?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You need to ask for recommendations, search on the internet, or look in the phone directory, and then make a call. You need to say "Could I check availability for your venue please?", then ask "What business facilities do you have?" and "How many people can the room or venue hold?" You could ask "Can you provide hospitality?" – that’s things like food and drink. Finally, don't forget to ask "How much does it cost?"

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks, there's a lot to ask. Hi Denise, I've got to book a venue for our plastic aubergine launch. Have you any ideas?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well, my friend Marge works for a hotel company that has conference facilities. You could give her a call. Look, here's her number.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, thanks Denise. Let's give it a try… 0–2–0–7–5–6–9–2.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Hello, the Pitz Hotel. Margery speaking.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh hi, this is Anna from Tip Top Trading, I'm a friend of Denise's.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Oh hi Anna. I've heard all about you. What are you ringing for?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I need to check availability for your venue for a product launch we’re doing.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Right! Well, I'm sure I can help. We do have a conference room. When is it for?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: This Friday.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Friday! This Friday? Well… that's a bit tricky: the room is being decorated at the moment.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: But we do have a smaller room that you could use – it's got a lovely view of the car park.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see… and how many people does it hold?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: You could easily squeeze in about 20 people.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: 20 people. I guess it will have to do. Do you have any business facilities – somewhere to plug in the laptop, projector, wi-fi, that sort of thing?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Oh yes, yes, we're very hi-tech. We even have a fax machine!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And can you provide hospitality too?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Of course! We do a 'business platter' consisting of orange juice, sandwiches, canapés – that really means cheese and pineapple on sticks.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I wonder, can you also provide Belgian chocolate biscuits?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: I'm sure we can.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's great! OK… and most importantly, how much does it cost?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Well, to book the room for 2 hours usually costs £1,000. The hospitality is extra but as you're a friend of Denise, I'll throw it in for nothing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You'll throw the food and drink in?! Won't that get messy?

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: No - I mean we'll provide it for free. Just don't tell anyone, otherwise everyone will expect it!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, that's fantastic Marge. Thanks. If you can send us an invoice, we'll sort payment out as soon as possible.

transcript.speaker: Marge
transcript.text: Bye Anna, and tell Denise I'll see her for our Zumba class tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna has saved the day again. The launch party for the plastic aubergine can now go ahead. If you're trying to book a venue for a business meeting or product launch, here are some of the phrases you could use:
Could I check availability for your venue please?
What business facilities do you have?
How many people can the room or venue hold?
Can you provide hospitality?
How much does it cost?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: So Anna, was Marge any help?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes. She found me a room and gave me a good deal. We just need to invite our clients now.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I can do that. I think it’s best if I call them - there's no time to post out invitations.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Good idea.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: But I just need to give Marge a call first, just to check a few things.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Typical Denise. Nothing's more urgent than talking to Marge!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: He can talk! If you need something doing it seems like Anna is the woman you need. Find out what else she is capable of in the next episode of English at Work. Bye!
